description:
Become a Better Writer: https://www.writerscience.com/newsletter/

Work with Me

✅ 1-to-1 Writing Feedback
https://www.writerscience.com/work-with-me/

Struggling to write dialogue that feels real? You’re not alone.

Even if you’re following all the classic writing advice, dialogue can still sound stiff, unnatural, or over-explained — and that’s exactly what we’re fixing today.

In this video, I’ll show you how to write engaging, authentic dialogue that actually sounds human, the kind of dialogue that brings your characters to life and pulls readers into the scene. These techniques apply whether you’re writing fiction, memoir, screenplays, or essays.

As an English professor, I’ve seen even talented students trip over the same pitfalls — but once you understand the three key principles in this video, you’ll be writing dialogue like a pro. Plus, I’ll break down one of the greatest examples of silent dialogue ever written: the church scene in There Will Be Blood.

🎬 Featured Examples:
 • There Will Be Blood (written & directed by Paul Thomas Anderson)
 • Carrie by Stephen King
 • All the Pretty Horses by Cormac McCarthy
 • A House for Mr. Biswas by V.S. Naipaul

Plus, if you’re obsessed with the art and science of expert writing, you’ll love my free newsletter Writer Science — packed with craft tips, storytelling breakdowns, and practical tools.
📩 Subscribe here → https://www.writerscience.com/newsletter

💬 Comment below: In There Will Be Blood, what do you think Daniel Plainview says to Eli Sunday after the baptism?
